tagline: Along the Canadian line, under the northern lights.
intro: Out of International Falls, nicknamed the Icebox of the Nation, Highway 11 heads west along the Rainy River to Baudette with Canada just across the water. From there it skirts Lake of the Woods to Warroad and Roseau and runs on across the top of the state toward North Dakota, through woods and farmland.

The dancing sky is the aurora borealis, which turns up often this far north, where there are few city lights to wash it out. Between Baudette and Warroad the roadsides bloom with wildflowers, lady's slippers among them.

moments.title: Baudette
moments.text: When fire took most of Baudette in 1910, many of its people got away in boxcars that a train pulled across the river to Rainy River, Ontario.

moments.title: Zippel Bay State Park
moments.text: Wilhelm Zippel's fishing village is down to foundations and hollows in the ground, but the park keeps a three-mile white sand beach on Lake of the Woods.

moments.title: Warroad
moments.text: Named for the old war road the Sioux followed down to the mouth of the Warroad River, the town on Muskeg Bay now answers to Hockeytown USA.
